title: Sicilian caponata
intro: Sweet-and-sour fried eggplant with celery, olives and capers. Better the next day.

steps.t: Cut the eggplants into 2 cm cubes, salt them and leave in a colander for 30 minutes, then pat dry.
steps.label: Salt

steps.t: Fry the eggplant in 4 tbsp of the oil, in batches, for 8 minutes, until golden and soft.
steps.label: Eggplant

oven.t: Toss the eggplant with 4 tbsp oil and roast at 220 °C for 25 minutes, turning halfway.

steps.t: In the same pan, soften the chopped onion and celery in the remaining oil for 8 minutes.
steps.label: Base

steps.t: Add the passata, olives, capers and pine nuts and simmer over medium heat for 10 minutes.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Pour in the vinegar and sugar and let the vinegar cook off for 2 minutes.
steps.label: Sweet-sour

steps.t: Return the eggplant, stir and cook 5 minutes more; take off the heat and add torn basil.
steps.label: Combine

steps.t: Let it rest for at least 1 hour and serve at room temperature.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Covered in the fridge it keeps 4 days and improves; take it out 30 minutes before serving.
Palermo style: 1 tsp unsweetened cocoa with the vinegar, and toasted almonds instead of pine nuts.

title: Roman-style artichokes
intro: Whole artichokes braised with mint and garlic, tender right down the stem.

steps.t: Snap off the tough outer leaves down to the pale ones, trim the tips and peel the stem, leaving 5 cm.
Drop each artichoke into water with the lemon juice; open the center and scoop out any choke.
Chop the mint, parsley and garlic with salt and pepper, stuff the centers and rub the rest over the outside.
Stand them head down, tightly packed in a tall pot; add the oil and water and season with salt.
Cover and cook over low heat for 30 minutes, until a knife slides easily into the base.
steps.label: Braise

pressure.t: Seal the pressure cooker and cook 8 minutes at high pressure on low heat, then release and test with a knife.

steps.t: Let them rest in the pot for 10 minutes and serve warm with the cooking juices.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Put a sheet of wet parchment under the lid to trap the steam so they don't dry out.
Cut leftovers into wedges for a frittata or bruschetta.

title: Padrón peppers
intro: Blistered little green peppers with flaky salt: most are mild, a few bite back.

steps.t: Wash the peppers and dry them very thoroughly so the oil doesn't spit.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan over high heat until shimmering.

bbq.t: Get the barbecue very hot and toss the peppers in the oil.

steps.t: Add the peppers in a single layer and toss for 4 minutes, until blistered and charred in spots.
steps.label: Pan-fry

bbq.t: Grill them in a grill basket over high heat for 5 minutes, turning, until blistered.

steps.t: Drain briefly on paper, sprinkle with salt and serve right away.

tips.t: For a round of tapas, serve with bacon-wrapped dates.
Add a dusting of smoked paprika or lemon zest with the salt.

title: Leeks vinaigrette
intro: A French bistro classic: tender leeks with a sharp mustard vinaigrette.

steps.t: Trim the roots and dark green tops, slit the tops and rinse well between the layers.
Cook in boiling salted water for 10 minutes, until a knife slides easily into the white part.
steps.label: Leeks

steam.t: Steam them for 15 minutes, until a knife slides easily into the white part.

steps.t: Drain and leave on a towel to drip and cool for 10 minutes, then halve lengthwise.
steps.label: Drain

steps.t: Whisk the mustard, vinegar and salt, then drizzle in the oil until thick; stir in the minced shallot.
Lay the leeks on a plate, spoon over the vinaigrette and finish with parsley and pepper.

tips.t: Dress them while still warm so they soak up the vinaigrette.
Grate a hard-boiled egg over the top for the classic "leeks mimosa".

title: Stuffed mushrooms
intro: Mushroom caps baked with a crisp filling of the stems, breadcrumbs and Parmesan.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Wipe the mushrooms clean, pull out the stems and chop them finely.

airfryer.t: Wipe the mushrooms clean, pull out the stems and chop them finely.

steps.t: Sauté the stems with the garlic in 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes, until the liquid has evaporated.
steps.label: Stems

steps.t: Off the heat, mix in the breadcrumbs, Parmesan, chopped parsley, salt, pepper and 1 tbsp oil.
Fill the caps, set them in an oiled dish and drizzle with the remaining oil.
Bake for 20 minutes, until golden on top and tender. Serve hot.
steps.label: Bake

airfryer.t: Air-fry at 180 °C for 12 minutes, until golden and tender.

tips.t: Add 80 g crumbled Italian sausage, browned with the stems, to the filling.
A little fresh thyme or marjoram in the filling works beautifully.
Stuff them in the morning, keep them chilled and bake just before serving.

title: Papa a la huancaína
intro: Boiled potatoes under a creamy sauce of fresh cheese and yellow chili.

steps.t: Boil the whole potatoes in their skins in salted water until tender but not falling apart.
steps.label: Potatoes

steps.t: Meanwhile hard-boil the eggs: 9 minutes in boiling water, then into cold water.
steps.label: Eggs

steps.t: Roughly chop the seeded pepper and chili, the onion and garlic, and sauté in 1 tbsp oil until soft.
steps.label: Sauté

steps.t: Blend with the cheese, evaporated milk, crackers, turmeric and remaining oil to a thick, smooth sauce.
Taste and add salt: if it's too runny add a cracker, if too thick a splash of milk.
Peel the warm potatoes and cut them into thick slices.
Line plates with lettuce, top with the potatoes, cover with sauce and garnish with egg halves and olives.

tips.t: With 3 tbsp ají amarillo paste instead of the pepper, chili and turmeric, it's the real Huancayo sauce.
Andean queso fresco is sold in Latin shops; Italian primo sale is the closest swap.
Leftover sauce keeps 2 days in the fridge: great with anticuchos or boiled eggs.

title: Zaalouk, eggplant and tomato salad
intro: Eggplant and tomato slow-cooked with cumin and paprika, scooped up with bread.

steps.t: Peel the eggplants in alternate stripes and cut them into 2 cm cubes.

oven.t: Heat the oven to 220 °C, prick the whole eggplants with a fork and set them on a baking tray.

steps.t: Steam them for 15 minutes, until very soft.
steps.label: Eggplant

oven.t: Roast at 220 °C for 40 minutes, until collapsed; then split them and scoop out the flesh.

steps.t: Meanwhile halve the tomatoes and grate them on the coarse side of a box grater, discarding the skins.
Heat the oil in a wide pan, add the tomatoes, crushed garlic, spices and salt and cook until the sauce thickens.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Add the eggplant, mash it with a fork and cook, stirring, until the oil rises and the mixture is thick.
steps.label: Zaalouk

steps.t: Turn off the heat and stir in the chopped cilantro, parsley and lemon juice. Serve warm or cold with a drizzle of oil.

tips.t: Scoop it up with khobz, Moroccan bread, as with all the cooked salads.
Don't rush it: it's ready when the oil separates at the edges and it looks almost like jam.
It's even better the next day and keeps 3 days in the fridge.

title: Pai huanggua, smashed cucumber salad
intro: Cucumbers smashed with a cleaver and dressed with garlic, black vinegar and chilli oil.

steps.t: Lay the cucumbers on a board and smash them with the flat of a wide knife until they split. Cut into 3 cm pieces.
Toss with the salt in a colander and leave them to release their water.
steps.label: Salt

steps.t: Meanwhile mix the finely minced garlic, vinegar, soy, sugar, chilli oil and sesame oil.
Drain the cucumbers, toss with the dressing and serve straight away, chilled, with coriander leaves.

tips.t: Smashed rather than sliced, the cucumbers have ragged edges that grab the dressing.
Dress them only at the last minute: after an hour they lose their crunch.

title: İmam bayıldı, stuffed aubergines
intro: Aubergines filled with onion and tomato, braised in olive oil and served lukewarm.

steps.t: Peel the aubergines in alternate stripes, leaving the stalk. Salt them and leave for 20 minutes to draw out the bitter juices.
steps.label: Salting

steps.t: Meanwhile slice the onions into thin half-moons, the garlic into slivers and the peppers into rings. Dice 2 tomatoes and slice 1.
Rinse and dry the aubergines. Fry them whole in 6 tbsp oil, turning, until soft and golden all over.
steps.label: Aubergines

oven.t: Brush the whole aubergines with oil and roast at 200 °C for 25 minutes, turning halfway, until soft.

steps.t: In the same pan, cook the onions in 4 tbsp oil over low heat for 10 minutes, until soft and sweet.
steps.label: Onions

steps.t: Add the garlic, peppers (keep a few rings back), diced tomatoes, tomato paste, sugar and salt. Cook 5 minutes, then add the parsley.
steps.label: Filling

steps.t: Lay the aubergines in a wide pan, slit them lengthways and open a pocket. Fill them and top with tomato and pepper.
Pour the hot water and remaining oil around them, cover and cook over low heat for 30 minutes, until meltingly soft.
steps.label: Braise

oven.t: Pour the hot water and remaining oil around them, cover with foil and bake at 180 °C for 40 minutes.

steps.t: Let them cool in the pan for at least 1 hour: serve at room temperature, even better the next day.
steps.label: Cool

tips.t: Striped peeling keeps the aubergine whole as it cooks and lets the flavour in.
They keep 3 days in the fridge: take them out half an hour before, as fridge-cold dulls the flavour.
Serve with warm bread to mop up the oil, or with rice pilaf for a full meal.
